accessibility:
- **Landmarks:** the header, the nav, the page and the footer are the page's banner, navigation,
  main and contentinfo landmarks, and the aside a complementary one, as long as the frame sits at
  the top of the page. A development build warns when it sits inside a `main` or a sectioning
  element, where the header and footer stop being landmarks.
- **Names:** the nav is named "Sections" (`labels.nav`), since the `Navbar` in the header names
  its own navigation. The name leaves out the word "navigation", which the role says. A `Menu`
  in the nav keeps its `<aside>`, which inside a `<nav>` is a plain element unless it's named.
- **Skip link:** the first thing on the page, hidden until it has focus, moves focus to the page's
  `<main>` (WCAG 2.4.1).
- **Sticky header:** `scroll-padding-top` on the document keeps an in-page link's target and a
  focused element below the header (WCAG 2.4.11, technique C43).
- **The burger** is a button named "menu" (`labels.burger`), with `aria-expanded` saying whether
  the drawer is open, or from the breakpoint up whether the column is shown, and `aria-controls`
  naming the nav. The server can't know the width, so until the page hydrates the burger has no
  `aria-expanded` and shows its bars, and the first paint after hydration has both right.
- **The drawer** is modal by default: focus moves to its close button, Tab and Shift+Tab stay
  inside, the page doesn't scroll, the rest of the frame is inert, and Escape closes it while it's
  the topmost overlay, so a `Modal` opened from it closes first. Escape, the close button and a
  click on the backdrop hand focus back to the burger, and so does a press outside the drawer
  without `overlay`, before the press moves it to what was pressed. The close button is there for
  a touch screen reader user, who has no Escape key. It stays a navigation landmark rather than a
  dialog: the inert frame is what keeps assistive technology inside it, so keep the page's content
  inside the frame's parts.
- **A closed drawer and a collapsed column** are `visibility: hidden`, so their links are out of
  the Tab order and the accessibility tree before any script runs.
- **The icon rail** keeps every name: labels are visually hidden, never removed, and icons are
  `aria-hidden`. Each tooltip adds no `aria-describedby` and is `aria-hidden` itself, so the name
  isn't read twice. It shows on keyboard focus as well as hover, stays while the pointer moves
  onto it, and Escape hides it (WCAG 1.4.13). A section's button in the rail reports
  `aria-expanded="false"`, since the rail hides its list, and pressing it expands the column and
  opens the section.
- **Reflow:** at 320 pixels wide the nav is a drawer, so nothing scrolls sideways (WCAG 1.4.10).
- **Motion:** the drawer's slide, the backdrop's fade and the column's collapse don't play under
  `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
- **Forced colors:** the column keeps its divider, and the drawer gets a border on its open edge in
  place of its shadow.
- **Right to left:** the column sits on the right, and the drawer slides in from the right.
summary: The `AppFrame` component lays out an app's pages: a header across the top, a navigation column down the side, the page, and an aside and a footer, with the nav a drawer behind a burger on narrow screens. The header and the column stick while the document scrolls, and a skip link comes first. The layout is CSS, so the server renders it as the browser does. It holds two states, each yours to control: whether the drawer is open, and whether the column is collapsed. `AppFrame.Burger` and `useAppFrame()` toggle whichever applies at the current width.

parts.summary: The `AppFrame` component lays out an app's pages: a header across the top, a navigation column down the side, the page, and an aside and a footer, with the nav a drawer behind a burger on narrow screens. The header and the column stick while the document scrolls, and a skip link comes first. The layout is CSS, so the server renders it as the browser does. It holds two states, each yours to control: whether the drawer is open, and whether the column is collapsed. `AppFrame.Burger` and `useAppFrame()` toggle whichever applies at the current width.

props.name: children
props.description: The parts, each a direct child: `Header`, `Nav`, `Main`, `Aside` and `Footer`, in that order, since it's the Tab order. The frame reads the `id` of `Main` and `Nav` off its children for the skip link and the burger, so a part wrapped in a component of your own takes no `id` of its own. Put the frame at the top of the page, outside any `main` or sectioning element.

props.name: breakpoint
props.description: The width from which the nav is a column beside the page. Below it, the nav is a drawer the burger opens. The stylesheet switches the layout at Bulma's breakpoint, and the script reads the width at Bulma's default breakpoints, so a theme that moves Bulma's breakpoints moves the layout but not which state the burger toggles.

props.name: navOpen
props.description: Whether the drawer is open, below the breakpoint. With it, the state is yours: update it from `onNavOpenChange`. It has no effect from the breakpoint up, where the frame asks to close it.

props.name: defaultNavOpen
props.description: Whether the drawer starts open.

props.name: onNavOpenChange
props.description: Called with the state asked for: by the burger, `useAppFrame()`, Escape, a press outside, the close button, a followed link (see `AppFrame.Nav`'s `closeOnNavigate`), or the window being at or past the breakpoint while it's open, which closes it.

props.name: navCollapsed
props.description: Whether the column is collapsed, from the breakpoint up: out of view, or down to its icons with `AppFrame.Nav rail`. With it, the state is yours: update it from `onNavCollapsedChange`. It has no effect below the breakpoint, where the drawer always shows the whole nav.

props.name: defaultNavCollapsed
props.description: Whether the column starts collapsed.

props.name: onNavCollapsedChange
props.description: Called with the state asked for: by the burger, `useAppFrame()`, or a `Menu.Section`'s button in the collapsed rail, which expands it.

props.name: skipLink
props.description: Renders a skip link first, visible when it has focus, that moves focus to `AppFrame.Main`. Turn it off only for a page that has its own.

props.name: labels
props.type: { skipLink?: string; nav?: string; closeNav?: string; burger?: string }
props.description: The strings the frame renders. Each one left out keeps its English default.

props.description: Text color helper.

parts.catchAll: All standard HTML attributes and Bulma helper props

parts.summary: The navigation of an AppFrame: a column beside the page from the breakpoint up, and a drawer below it.

props.name: children
props.description: Usually a `Menu`. A nav taller than the window scrolls on its own, except a column collapsed to a rail, which doesn't (see `rail`). With `overlay`, the rest of the frame is inert while the drawer is open, so an overlay opened from the drawer, such as a `Modal`, goes inside the nav or renders outside the frame (Modal's `portal`).

props.name: width
props.description: The column's width, and the drawer's up to the window's width less a strip of backdrop. A number is pixels, and a string any CSS length. It writes `--bulma-app-frame-nav-width`, 16rem by default.

props.name: overlay
props.description: Shows a backdrop behind the drawer and makes it modal: Tab stays inside, the page scroll locks, and the rest of the frame is inert, while what renders outside it, such as a Modal opened from the drawer or a toast, stays live. Without it the drawer covers the page without holding Tab, and focus can move to the page beside it. Either way focus moves in as it opens. Sidebar's `overlay`.

props.name: closeOnEscape
props.description: Closes the drawer on Escape, while it's the topmost overlay, so Escape closes one layer at a time.

props.name: closeOnClickOutside
props.description: Closes the drawer on a press outside it while it's the topmost overlay: a click on the backdrop, or without `overlay` a press anywhere outside it. Focus goes back to the burger as it closes. Without `overlay`, the press's own mousedown then moves it, as on any page: to what was pressed if that takes focus, and otherwise off the burger to the page. A touch that scrolls leaves it on the burger. A press on a control whose `aria-controls` names the nav, such as the burger, is left to that control. Popover's `closeOnClickOutside`.

props.name: closeOnNavigate
props.description: Closes the drawer when a link inside it is followed with a plain click: not with a modifier key held, and not on a link with a `target` other than `_self` or a `download`. Only a link the nav holds in the page counts, not one in a Modal or a popup it portals elsewhere. Focus goes back to the burger, and the navigation takes it from there: a router that moves focus on navigation moves it, and an in-page `#` link leaves it at its target, as it does anywhere on the page. Turn it off for a drawer of filters rather than links.

props.name: rail
props.description: From the breakpoint up, a collapsed column shrinks to a rail of icons instead of leaving the page. The rail needs a `Menu` inside the nav: a Menu portaled out of it, such as one in a Popover or a Modal opened from it, isn't in the rail, nor is a `Menu.List` with no Menu around it, and a development build warns when a collapsed rail holds no Menu. Every top-level `Menu.Item` and `Menu.Section` needs an `icon`: in the rail, an item without one has nothing to show and its label spills over the page, and a section's button is blank, so a development build warns about one without. In the rail their labels are visually hidden, so each stays its link's or button's name, and shows in a `Tooltip` beside the rail on hover and keyboard focus. Nested lists and `Menu.Label` headings hide there, and a section's button expands the column and opens the section. Collapsed to the rail, the column doesn't scroll on its own, so a tooltip isn't clipped. It sticks under the header while it fits there. A rail taller than the window under the header scrolls with the page instead, so its lower icons come into view as the page scrolls and as Tab reaches them. That takes a measurement in the browser, so before the page hydrates such a rail sticks.

parts.summary: The button that opens the drawer, or collapses the column from the breakpoint up: Navbar.Burger, wired to the frame.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes.

props.name: textColor
props.description: Text color for the burger.

props.name: color
props.description: Renders `has-text-<color>`, exactly like `textColor`. Bulma has no `.navbar-burger.is-<color>` rule, so this is not a filled variant. `textColor` takes precedence when both are set, and is the one that reaches the full color list.

props.name: children
props.description: Custom content inside the burger, rendered after its four bar spans. Bulma styles every `<span>` in the burger as a bar, so an extra span here draws an extra bar.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name. Pass your own to replace it. An empty one, or a spread carrying `'aria-label': undefined`, keeps the default rather than leaving the button unnamed.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Click handler.

extraProps.name: ref
extraProps.description: Ref forwarded to the burger button element.

extraProps.name: type
extraProps.description: Button type. Defaults to `'button'`, so a burger inside a form does not submit it. Pass `'submit'` or `'reset'` and yours is used; any other value, or a spread carrying `type: undefined`, renders `'button'`.
